description: Single-user Svelte 5 + SvelteKit email inbox using Resend for inbound/outbound mail, Turso (libSQL/Drizzle) for persistence, Cloudflare R2 for attachments, one-button 6-digit-code auth, and a 'Dusk Terminal' dark-first design system, deployed to Vercel.

userStories.title: Scaffold SvelteKit project with Tailwind CSS and Vercel adapter
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a working SvelteKit project with Tailwind CSS and the Vercel adapter installed, so every later story has a real app to build inside.
acceptanceCriteria: SvelteKit project created with TypeScript, using Svelte 5 (runes enabled)
Tailwind CSS installed and configured (postcss/tailwind config present, imported in the root layout)
@sveltejs/adapter-vercel installed and set as the adapter in svelte.config.js
npm run dev starts successfully and renders a default placeholder page
npm run build completes successfully with the Vercel adapter
Typecheck/lint passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Scaffolded via `sv create` (prettier, eslint, tailwindcss, sveltekit-adapter=vercel add-ons). No svelte.config.js in this SvelteKit version — adapter/compiler options live in vite.config.ts instead. adapter-vercel given explicit runtime: 'nodejs22.x' since local Node (v26) is unsupported by its auto-detection. See docs/demos/US-A00.md for verification proof.

userStories.title: Provision Turso database and Drizzle schema scaffold
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the database provisioned and connected so all later features have persistence to build on.
acceptanceCriteria: Turso database created and TURSO_DATABASE_URL/TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN available locally via .env and in Vercel project settings
Drizzle ORM installed and configured with drizzle-orm/libsql and a drizzle.config.ts pointing at the Turso instance
npm run db:push (or equivalent) successfully applies an empty baseline schema
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Installed drizzle-orm, @libsql/client, drizzle-kit. Added src/lib/server/db/schema.ts (empty baseline module), src/lib/server/db/index.ts (drizzle(libsql) client), drizzle.config.ts (dialect: 'turso'), and npm scripts db:push/db:generate/db:studio. `npm run db:push --force` applied cleanly against the real Turso instance already provisioned in .env ('No changes detected' for the empty baseline). Full schema (contacts/threads/emails/attachments/auth_codes/sessions) is deferred to US-D01 per prd-data-model.md. See docs/demos/US-A01.md for verification proof.

userStories.title: Provision Cloudflare R2 for attachment storage
userStories.description: As a developer, I need object storage wired up so attachments have somewhere to live outside the database.
acceptanceCriteria: Cloudflare R2 bucket created (private, no public access/custom domain); R2_ACCOUNT_ID, R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID, R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, R2_BUCKET_NAME available locally and in Vercel project settings
A small utility function exists that uploads a Buffer/Blob to R2 (via the S3-compatible API) and returns its object key

A small utility function exists that generates a time-limited presigned GET URL for a given object key (used wherever the app needs to let the browser fetch/download an attachment, since the bucket is private)
A small utility function exists that deletes an R2 object by key
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Bucket is private (owner is not using a public bucket URL / custom domain), so there is no R2_PUBLIC_URL_BASE env var — access is via presigned URLs generated on demand instead of a static public URL. This affects attachments.r2_public_url in prd-data-model.md and the 'public URL' wording in US-E05/US-G03 acceptance criteria; those should be read as 'presigned URL generated at request time' rather than a stored permanent public URL. src/lib/server/r2/index.ts provides uploadToR2/deleteFromR2/getR2SignedDownloadUrl, verified end-to-end (upload, presigned fetch, delete, post-delete 404) against the real R2 bucket via scripts/verify-r2.mts. R2_ACCOUNT_ID/R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID/R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY/R2_BUCKET_NAME are set locally in .env; no vercel CLI/project link is available in this environment, so adding the same vars to the Vercel project's env settings is still an outstanding manual step for the project owner before deploying.

userStories.title: Scaffold protected route group and session-check layout
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the (app) route group to redirect unauthenticated visitors to /login, so every mailbox feature is protected from day one.
acceptanceCriteria: src/routes/(app)/+layout.server.ts checks for a valid session cookie and redirects to /login if absent/invalid
src/routes/login/+page.svelte renders a placeholder page (full auth UI built in a later story)
Visiting /inbox while unauthenticated redirects to /login
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: src/lib/server/auth/session.ts exports SESSION_COOKIE_NAME + hasSessionCookie (presence-only check; no sessions table yet, that's US-B01). src/routes/(app)/+layout.server.ts redirects to /login if the cookie is missing. Placeholder pages at src/routes/login/+page.svelte and src/routes/(app)/inbox/+page.svelte. Verified via curl (302 to /login unauthenticated, 200 with a fake session cookie) and rodney (unauthenticated /inbox visit lands on /login, screenshot in docs/demos/US-A03.md).

All specified indexes are created (emails.thread_id, emails.message_id unique, emails.is_read+is_deleted, threads.last_message_at, contacts.email unique, attachments.email_id, sessions.token_hash unique, auth_codes.expires_at)
Foreign keys (emails.thread_id, attachments.email_id) are enforced
Migration applies cleanly against a fresh Turso database
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: 'Send me a code' endpoint with rate limiting
userStories.description: As the app owner, I want clicking the login button to email me a 6-digit code, so I can authenticate without a password.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/auth/request-code generates a cryptographically random 6-digit code
The code is hashed (e.g., SHA-256) before storage; the raw code is never persisted
A row is inserted into auth_codes with expires_at = now + 10 minutes
The email is sent via Resend from auth@caseynazelrod.com to the constant AUTH_RECIPIENT_EMAIL (cwnaze@gmail.com) - this address is never read from request input
Rate limiting: no more than 3 code requests per 10-minute rolling window; the 4th+ request in that window returns 429 without sending an email or creating a new code row
Any previously unused, unexpired code is invalidated when a new one is requested (only one active code at a time)
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Verify-code endpoint and session creation
userStories.description: As the app owner, I want to enter the 6-digit code and be logged in, so I can access my inbox.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/auth/verify-code accepts a 6-digit code, hashes it, and compares against the active unexpired, unused auth_codes row
On match: marks the code row used_at = now(), creates a sessions row, and sets an httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax session cookie containing only an opaque session token
On mismatch: increments attempt_count; after 5 failed attempts against a given code, that code is invalidated and the user must request a new one
Expired codes are rejected with a clear error and do not increment attempt count against a dead code
A code cannot be used twice
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Login page UI - single button and code entry
userStories.description: As the app owner, I want a minimal login screen: one button, then a code field, so login is fast and matches the Dusk Terminal aesthetic.
acceptanceCriteria: /login renders centered app mark + single 'Send me a code' button (no email input field anywhere on the page)
Clicking the button calls the request-code endpoint and transitions the UI to a 6-digit code entry step (monospace input)
Submitting an incorrect code shows an inline error without navigating away
Submitting a valid code redirects to /inbox
Rate-limit (429) responses show a clear 'try again in N minutes' message
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill

userStories.title: Route protection and logout

A visible logout action exists in the app shell

userStories.title: Verify Resend inbound webhook signature
userStories.description: As a developer, I need every inbound webhook request cryptographically verified, so unauthenticated payloads can never be ingested.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/webhooks/resend-inbound reads svix-id, svix-timestamp, svix-signature headers
Uses the svix library and RESEND_INBOUND_WEBHOOK_SECRET to verify the raw request body

userStories.title: Parse inbound payload and upsert contact

A contacts row is upserted by email (case-insensitive); if new, name is set from the payload's display name and auto_created = true
If a contact already exists and was manually edited (auto_created = false), its name is not overwritten

userStories.title: Sanitize HTML body and store email

acceptanceCriteria: body_html is run through isomorphic-dompurify stripping scripts, event handlers, and disallowed remote-loading tags before being persisted
body_text (plain-text alternative) is stored as-is if present in the payload
Duplicate deliveries (same message_id already in emails) are detected and skipped (idempotent ingestion) rather than erroring

userStories.title: Thread assignment
userStories.description: As the app owner, I want replies grouped with their original conversation, so I see a coherent thread instead of scattered messages.
acceptanceCriteria: If the payload's In-Reply-To matches an existing emails.message_id, the new email is attached to that email's thread_id
If no match is found, a new threads row is created with the (normalized) subject
threads.last_message_at and threads.is_read are updated per the Data Model PRD rules
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Attachment extraction and R2 upload

An attachments row is created per file with filename, content-type, size, and R2 key (bucket is private; a presigned URL is generated on demand rather than stored)
Ingestion completes successfully even if one attachment upload fails, logging the failure without discarding the rest of the email
